title: Correction memory does not equal correction infusion
summary: A candidate cross-lane pattern: an institution can build a repository, database, recommendation system, or lessons-learned rail, while still failing to get the right lesson to the right decision point. The pattern is supported only as an infrastructure-audit pair in rev0017; it is not an indictment of any current system and not a mature theory.

status_history.note: Promoted from source-infrastructure observation using NASA LLIS plus historical GAO audit, with NTSB/Cochrane/registration rails as future comparators.

claims.claim: The cube needs to distinguish correction-memory surfaces from correction-infusion outcomes: NASA describes LLIS as an official reviewed lessons database and APPEL separates collect/record/disseminate/apply, while GAO’s historical audit shows that collection/sharing/use can remain weak even when the repository exists.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction or narrows its scope.

claims.claim: MKH-PAT-0014 remains candidate-level: it does not claim NASA LLIS is ineffective today, nor that all repositories fail; it asserts a record-design requirement that storage, retrieval, dissemination, application, and follow-through be represented separately.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction or narrows its scope.

evidence_profile.source_basis: one infrastructure record plus one historical government audit record; not yet cross-industry
limitations: No sample records tracing lesson-to-policy/practice paths.

type_payload.short_definition: A correction surface may preserve or publish lessons without those lessons reliably entering future decisions, processes, training, policy, or design controls.

case_evidence.mechanism: LLIS provides official reviewed public lessons/recommendation storage and search.
GAO historical audit found collection/sharing/use barriers, demonstrating why repository existence must be audited separately from infusion.

not_this: not a claim that lessons-learned repositories are useless
not a current-performance claim about NASA LLIS
not a replacement for outcome/follow-through records
needed_before_synthesis: Add at least two additional correction-memory systems and audits/outcome traces.
Add a positive control where a lesson demonstrably changed a decision/process before repeat harm.
Add a negative control where a repository did work well enough to prevent recurrence.

positive_controls_needed: A source-backed case where a lesson/recommendation repository or action-tracking system measurably changed a process, checklist, design, or policy before recurrence.
negative_controls_needed: A correction-memory system with high documented uptake and effective application, to avoid assuming repositories fail by default.
counterexamples_to_seek: A domain where formal lessons learned demonstrably outperform informal mentorship/story transmission on timely application.
rollback_triggers: A newer audit shows the infrastructure-audit distinction is already sufficiently represented elsewhere in the cube.
Second-pass review finds GAO 2001 inapplicable to the general pattern beyond historical NASA context.
Pattern scope becomes too broad and must split into retrieval, incentive, and application subpatterns.

maturity_gate.minimum_before_mature: At least three systems, one current audit/outcome trace, one positive control, one negative control, and explicit split/merge decision.

handling_notes: Do not use “lessons not learned” as a snide slogan; encode the actual transfer surfaces and barriers.
Separate institutional design critique from blame against individuals.

unknowns: Whether this should be a pattern candidate or a method rule only.
How to measure infusion across domains without hindsight bias.
What positive/negative controls best calibrate the pattern.
next_actions: Trace one source-backed lesson from repository to policy/procedure/action.
Add current NASA LLIS audit or usage source if available.
